item.title: Return of the Wild: A Lewis and Clark Wildlife Resurvey — Thu Oct 8, 7:00 PM — North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences
item.description:
Two hundred and twenty years after Lewis and Clark documented the animals of the west in their journals, we retraced their route with camera traps to find out what we lost, what’s still there, and what it took to save America’s wildlife. Dr. Roland Kays, head of the Biodiversity Research Lab at NCMNS and professor at NC State University, will share the story of his team’s expedition across the United States in this special lecture event.
Doors open at 6:30PM. The lecture begins in the WRAL 3D Theater at 7PM. This event is free and open to the public.
More info: https://ncmns.net/return-of-the-wild
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: CCN Colloquium: "Facing Down the Interface Problem: No Distinctive Cost to Representational Diversity" — Fri Oct 9, 12:00 PM — LSRC - DIBS B035 Multipurpose Room
item.description: Abstract: Mental states represent the world in systematically different ways, encoding contents in multiple "codes" or "formats." For example, some mental states are thought to be image-like, others sentence-like; some analog, others symbolic. The interface problem concerns how agents can coordinate contents across different mental codes. The standard assumption is that interfaces incur distinctive costs: translation from one format to another is explanatorily mysterious and computationally difficult. I argue that there is no reason to think that between-format representational transitions, or "translations," are distinctively more challenging to explain or to execute than within-format transitions, or "inferences." In fact, translation and inference can exemplify similar properties and fulfill similar functions. item.title: Pressing Prompts Community Conversation (Online) — Fri Oct 9, 12:00 PM — Virtual
item.description:
Incubated at Duke, Pressing Prompts (pressingprompts.org) is an open education resource for instructors across all disciplines who are seeking ways to integrate AI ethics into their classrooms. Unlike a static set of "best practices," Pressing Prompts is grounded in principles of critical pedagogy and educational experimentation, encouraging instructors and students to examine how AI raises crucial questions about our academic responsibilities, knowledge, labor, judgment, and learning.
In this community conversation, we will spend time hearing from faculty who have experimented with Pressing Prompts in their classrooms, answer questions and brainstorm together about how you might integrate the resource into your pedagogy, and learn from faculty about interest in and ideas for iterating Pressing Prompts for future use.
Source: Duke University

item.title: Mesh-LLM & Trusting a Stranger's Machine, Part 2: Evidence You Can Check — Mon Oct 12, 5:00 PM
item.description:
All Things AI (Live) When a stranger's machine serves an AI request, how can the requester check what happened? We'll show mesh-llm's Evidence plugin recording signed, hash-chained evidence on each node and sending each side's signed record to the other.
A demo build will show both-sides confirmation and a paid Lightning exchange; we'll label the build and distinguish it from a released version. I'll show a TRACE record alongside the exchange capsule to explain what additional runtime evidence, including hardware evidence when available, can establish. We'll also show the limits: the plugin's node keys are self-attested, and its referee applies once mesh-llm marks twins.
Source: Meetup: All Things AI

item.title: Rennie Harris Puremovement American Dance Theater — Fri Oct 16, 8:00 PM — UNCG Auditorium
item.description:
Rennie Harris Puremovement American Dance Theater (RHPM) is the leading US street dance theater company, and for over thirty-five years has been dedicated to preserving and disseminating hip-hop aesthetics and street dance culture through workshops, classes, history, lecture demonstrations, long-term residencies, mentoring programs, and public performances. With his roots in the inner-city, Harris and RHPM present unique stories that are riveting, intimate, and honest. RHPM’s mission is to re-educate the public about hip-hop culture and street dance through its artistic work, sharing the essence and spirit of street dance, rather than the commercially exploited stereotype portrayed by the media.
Dr. Lorenzo “Rennie” Harris is a leading ambassador for hip-hop. Harris grew up entrenched in hip-hop culture in all its forms—music, dance, language. Throughout his career, he has embraced the culture and sought to honor its legacy, believing that hip-hop and street dance is the purest form

item.title: Native Tree Planting (Cornelius) — Sat Oct 24, 9:00 AM
item.description: Join NCWF Lake Norman Wildlife Chapter to plant native trees in Cornelius as part of North Carolina Wildlife Federation’s Clean and Green program. Back in April, NCWF Lake Norman Wildlife Chapter and the Town of Cornelius hosted its annual Clean & Green trash cleanup event. Town staff and volunteers from the Society of Women Engineers, Safe Harbor – Kings Point Marina, and Lake Norman Wildlife took to the land and the lake to remove hundreds of pounds of trash and debris. North Carolina Wildlife Federation is committed to planting one native tree for every 25 pounds of trash collected statewide. Removing litter protects wildlife from possible entanglement, strangulation, and ingestion while improving water quality and removing toxins from the environment. This year we will plant native trees at Bailey Road Park. item.title: John and June Allcott Gallery: taylor barnes, Weight of Light — Thu Oct 29, 8:00 AM — Hanes Art Center
item.description:
Reception and gallery talk: October 29, 2026, 5:00 pm
Weight of Light explores how powerful emotions can be expressed through simplicity. Using bold contrasts between light and dark, the artist creates striking images that convey feeling through form, space, and gesture rather than detailed storytelling. The exhibition invites viewers to slow down and experience mood, tension, and vulnerability in a direct and deeply human way.
Weight of Light brings together seven works created by artist taylor barnes during her year-long residency at West Orchid in Pine Lake, Georgia. The work marks a period of experimentation and personal reflection. Drawing from her background in fibers and ceramics, barnes approaches the canvas as a site of material exploration. Through processes of staining, layering, and transforming solids into liquids and back again, she creates environments that make space for chance, absence, and emergence. item.title: Rethinking Seasonal Cleanup: Why Less Can Be More for Wildlife (in person) — Tue Nov 10, 12:00 PM — Duke Gardens–Pelham-Cullen Classroom in the Barnes Welcome Center
item.description: Are you unsure about when to cut back dormant plants or how many leaves to leave behind? Perhaps you’ve heard about stem-nesting bees or insects that overwinter in fallen foliage and want to support them. Traditional garden practice dictated raking leaves and cutting everything back to “tidy up” before winter. Today, delaying cutbacks and leaving fallen leaves has become more common as gardeners appreciate plants’ unique winter beauty and prioritize wildlife. The best approach depends on your landscape goals and priorities, and this session will help you navigate seasonal cutbacks and leaf management. Join Shannon Currey, education and outreach at Izel Native Plants, to learn strategies that support local wildlife while maintaining a landscape that looks cared for and intentional. This description is for the in-person attendance option—register separately to attend virtually. Fee: Free; registration required. Parking: Parking fees apply. item.title: Opting Out of Integrated AI — Wed Nov 11, 11:00 AM
item.description:
This workshop, led by University Library staff, will explore strategies for using AI more intentionally. We will discuss topics ranging from browser tracking to the role of AI tools in your everyday life. We will also introduce practical ways to take more control of when or how those tools are used, how your data are collected and tracked, and ways you can opt out. At the end of the workshop, we will share additional resources for learning more about AI and adopting a more mindful approach to AI in our world.
This workshop is offered by the University Library and will be led by librarians Dayna Durbin and Gracie Riehm.
This workshop is being offered remotely via Zoom only. You can register through the library calendar. Registrants will receive a Zoom link; those on the waitlist will not receive a Zoom link unless they are bumped up to a registered spot.
All registrants however, will receive access to the meeting recording and resources.
